newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to maintain 65 pct tariff on refined sugar.
newsitem.headline: Manila to maintain 65 pct tariff on refined sugar.

text.p: The Philippines will maintain the 65 percent tariff on refined sugar imported from neighbouring Southeast Asian countries, a senior official said on Friday.
Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa told reporters the plan has been approved by the Cabinet of President Fidel Ramos.
The Philippines was set to drop the tariff on sugar imports starting on July 1 as part of its commitment to the World Trade Organisation.
However, the 35 percent rebate accorded to southeast Asian refined sugar imports would be removed.
Tariff on refined sugar imports from non-ASEAN countries is to be cut to 65 percent from 100 percent, he added.
"Starting July 1, tariff on refined sugar from Southeast Asian countries will be maintained but sugar tariff on other types of sugar will be dropped," Gamboa said.
Tariff on raw sugar would be cut to 60 percent from the present 100 percent. This is lower than the earlier 80 percent committed by Manila to the World Trade Organisation starting July 1.
